title: H100 profile benchmark results (baseline vs tuned) — first pass
content:
Sheet purpose
- Capture baseline vs tuned deltas for the H100 profile across the current workload matrix.
- This is NOT a marketing artifact. Use for engineering validation + perf-canary gate tuning.

Builds / configs compared
- Baseline: runtime=1.18.2 (prod-ish), profiles=disabled, kernel_autoselect=default, scheduler=adaptive defaults
- Tuned (Balanced): runtime=1.19.0-rc3 + profile_pack=h100/v0.3.0, profile=h100-balanced, kernel_autoselect=h100-seq-buckets (PR-22008), scheduler_preset=balanced (PR-22003)
- Tuned (Throughput-first): runtime=1.19.0-rc3 + profile_pack=h100/v0.3.0, profile=h100-throughput-first, scheduler_preset=throughput_first (PR-22003)

Test environment (runner)
- GPU: NVIDIA H100 SXM 80GB (single GPU per node), persistence mode on
- Driver/CUDA: 550.54 / CUDA 12.4
- Host: AMD EPYC 7xx3, 512GB RAM, NVMe scratch
- Network: single-node; NCCL/collectives not exercised (note: multi-GPU tuned profile pending)
- Runtime flags held constant unless noted by profile: streaming=on for streaming workloads, log_level=warn
- Duration: 12–15 min per workload point; report medians across 5 steady-state windows

Metric definitions
- TTFT p50/p95 (ms): time-to-first-token (streaming) or time-to-first-byte (non-streaming)
- Decode tok/s: steady-state decode throughput per GPU (excluding prefill), measured at server
- E2E tok/s: end-to-end tokens/sec per GPU across prefill+decode (useful for cost)
- Retry %: fraction of requests retried due to transient admission/backpressure or internal timeout
- OOM: count of OOM events observed in run
- GPU mem (GB): peak device memory during steady state (nvml peak)

Workload matrix keys (abbrev)
- Model: R7B = Redwood-7B chat, R13B = Redwood-13B instruct, R34B = Redwood-34B instruct
- Len bucket: S=prompt 128–512 / gen 128; M=prompt 1k–2k / gen 256; L=prompt 4k–8k / gen 512; XL=prompt 16k / gen 256 (long-context)
- Concurrency: number of simultaneous in-flight requests (server-side)
- Pattern: stream=token streaming, batch=non-streaming

Tab: Summary deltas (Balanced vs Baseline)
- Overall: +6% to +18% decode tok/s improvements on S/M buckets; mixed on L/XL depending on fairness pressure; TTFT p95 unchanged to slightly better in most streaming cases; one tail regression observed at high concurrency + long prompts before PR-22033 (not in this build).

Tab: Aggregates (rolled-up)
- Weighted average (streaming workloads only; weights = request mix 40% S, 35% M, 20% L, 5% XL):
  - Balanced vs Baseline: TTFT p50 -3.8%, TTFT p95 -1.2%, Decode tok/s +11.5%, Retry +0.1pp, GPU mem +0.4GB
  - Throughput-first vs Baseline: TTFT p50 +2.1%, TTFT p95 +18.4%, Decode tok/s +20.8%, Retry +2.2pp, GPU mem +0.6GB

Notes / interpretation
1) Balanced is safe default for Hosted/Dedicated H100 pools
- Gains are consistent in S/M buckets (where most traffic sits) without moving p95 in a meaningful way.
- Retry rate stays roughly flat; any increase is within current oncall tolerance.

2) Throughput-first is opt-in and needs guardrails
- It consistently boosts decode tok/s but tends to increase p95 TTFT and retries at moderate-to-high concurrency.
- Recommendation: keep behind per-pool override; require perf-canary green at target conc and add explicit rollback threshold (retry% + tail).

3) Kernel seq-len buckets appear to be doing the expected thing
- Largest wins show up in S/M; on L/XL, improvements are smaller and scheduler fairness dominates tail behavior.
- No correctness issues observed; outputs validated by hash of first 32 tokens across 200 sampled prompts (no drift beyond nondeterminism).

4) Memory impact
- H100 80GB has headroom; tuned profiles add minor overhead (+0.3–0.6GB peak) likely from larger KV-cache reservation behavior.
- No OOMs in this sheet. Note: OOM coverage is handled more aggressively on L40S; H100 tests here are not stress-to-failure.

Open questions / TODO (next iteration)
- Add multi-GPU node runs (tensor-parallel) to exercise NCCL tuning assumptions.
- Add a tool-calling prompt slice (Applied ML request) to capture bursty decode patterns.
- Re-run W6/W7/W10 at conc=48 and conc=24 to better map the “knee” for p95 TTFT.
- Confirm results after PR-22033 lands (tail regression fix for prefill/decode fairness); this sheet is pre-merge.

Proposed perf-canary gates (draft)
- Balanced: allow +3% TTFT p95 drift on streaming S/M buckets, require >= +6% decode tok/s uplift overall, retry% <= baseline +0.5pp
- Throughput-first: require explicit opt-in label; gate on retry% <= baseline +2.0pp and TTFT p95 <= baseline +12% (or reject)
